common_name: quad set contraction patella kneecap VMO
why: Isometrically activates the VMO (inner quad) to correct kneecap tracking without joint loading — safest first step for kneecap pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit/Lie):** Sit or lie with leg straight. Place rolled towel under knee. **STEP 2 (Tighten):** Tighten quadriceps, pressing back of knee into towel. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 10 seconds, fully relax 5 seconds.
process: 15 reps x 3 sets. Do this before any kneecap exercise.

common_name: straight leg raise knee patella kneecap
why: Builds VMO and quad strength with zero knee bend — safe even in acute kneecap pain or patellar tendinopathy.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. Bend one knee, keep other straight. **STEP 2 (Tighten):** Tighten straight leg quad (pull toes toward you). **STEP 3 (Lift):** Raise straight leg to height of bent knee. Hold 3 seconds. Lower slowly.

common_name: medial VMO inner knee isometric strengthening
why: Isolates vastus medialis oblique (inner quad) which stabilises inner knee and medial collateral ligament.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit in chair, knees bent 90 degrees. Place ball between inner thighs. **STEP 2 (Squeeze):** Squeeze ball with thighs — focus on feeling inner knee area work. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 10 seconds. Relax.

common_name: IT band outer knee stretch iliotibial
why: Reduces tension in the iliotibial band at its insertion on the outer knee (Gerdy's tubercle) — primary cause of lateral knee pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Stand and cross right leg behind left. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Push right hip out to side and lean upper body left. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull along outer right knee and thigh. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: hamstring stretch behind knee popliteus
why: Lengthens hamstrings and popliteus at back of knee — relieves tightness and pain behind the knee common after kneeling.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand, place heel on low step. **STEP 2 (Hinge):** Hinge forward from hips with flat back. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel pull at back of knee. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: patellar mobilisation kneecap glide patella
why: Manually moves kneecap in all four directions to break adhesions and restore smooth patellar tracking — reduces catching and grinding.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Relax):** Sit with leg straight, quadriceps fully relaxed. **STEP 2 (Grip):** Place fingertips on outer edges of kneecap. **STEP 3 (Glide):** Gently push kneecap medially 10 times, then laterally 10 times, then up and down.

common_name: supine hamstring popliteus behind knee stretch
why: Stretching the popliteus reduces aching tightness and clicking behind the knee.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Lie):** Lie on back. Loop towel or band around foot. **STEP 2 (Lift):** Use towel to lift leg, straightening knee as much as comfortable. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 30 seconds. Slightly internally rotate foot for popliteus focus.

common_name: lateral foam roll IT band outer knee
solution_stretch: IT Band Foam Roll — Outer Knee
why: Reduces adhesions in the distal IT band at the outer knee where repetitive-use inflammation concentrates.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Side lie):** Lie on side, foam roller under outer thigh. **STEP 2 (Roll):** Slowly roll from outer hip to just above outer knee. **STEP 3 (Pause):** Stop on tender spots for 20-30 seconds.

common_name: knee circle warmup patella popliteus
why: Gently mobilises tibiofemoral and patellofemoral joints to increase synovial fluid before loading.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand feet together, hands on knees. **STEP 2 (Circle):** Make slow large circles with knees — 10 clockwise. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** 10 counter-clockwise.
process: 10 each direction. Start small, build to full range.

common_name: terminal knee extension VMO patella kneecap
why: The most precise VMO exercise — trains only last 15 degrees of knee extension where VMO is most active for kneecap control.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Band):** Anchor band behind you at knee height. Loop it around back of knee. **STEP 2 (Bend):** Bend knee slightly (15 degrees). **STEP 3 (Extend):** Fully straighten knee against band. Hold 2 seconds.

common_name: step up knee patella quad femor
why: Functional knee strengthener that trains quad and glutes in a stair-climbing pattern — directly improves kneecap tracking.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Step):** Place right foot on low step. **STEP 2 (Press):** Push through right heel to step up. **STEP 3 (Control):** Lower left foot back slowly. Focus on knee tracking over second toe.

common_name: hero pose knee patella yoga reclined
why: Gently stretches quadriceps passively, reducing compressive forces on kneecap by lengthening patellar tendon.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Kneel):** Kneel on soft surface, shins down. **STEP 2 (Sit):** Sit back between heels. **STEP 3 (Recline):** Only if comfortable, lean back on hands. Hold 1 minute.
process: 1 minute hold. Place folded blanket under knees if painful.

common_name: knee tracking squat patella kneecap posture
why: Retrains kneecap to track straight over second toe — corrects inward-knee collapse that strains inner structures.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Box):** Stand in front of low chair. **STEP 2 (Squat):** Slowly lower to chair, watching kneecap stay over second toe. **STEP 3 (Rise):** Press through heel to rise without knee caving inward.
process: 15 slow reps x 2 sets. Use mirror to check knee alignment.

common_name: standing calf gastrocnemius stretch
why: Lengthens gastrocnemius from knee to heel — relieves cramping tightness and post-exercise calf aching.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand facing wall. Place right foot back, leg straight, heel down. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean body forward through front leg until pull in middle of right calf. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 30-45 seconds.

common_name: seated soleus lower calf stretch ankle
why: Stretches the soleus (deeper calf) which only opens when knee is bent — relieves lower calf and Achilles tightness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit on chair, one foot flat on floor. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean knee forward over toes — keep heel on floor. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch deep in lower calf above heel. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: eccentric heel drop achilles calf tendon
why: The clinically proven first intervention for Achilles tendinopathy — eccentric loading reduces inflammation and remodels tendon safely.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Edge):** Stand with ball of foot on step edge, heel over edge. **STEP 2 (Rise):** Use both legs to rise onto tiptoes. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Shift weight to affected leg and SLOWLY lower heel below step level. Take 3 full seconds.
process: 15 reps x 3 sets TWICE daily. Mild pain (up to 5/10) acceptable during eccentric phase.

common_name: towel achilles stretch calf towel
why: Gentle passive Achilles and calf stretch — safe for acute Achilles pain where weight-bearing stretch is too painful.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with leg straight. Loop towel around ball of foot. **STEP 2 (Pull):** Gently pull towel toward you to bring foot upward. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 30 seconds. No bouncing.

common_name: dorsiflexion calf ankle stretch
why: Specifically targets tight upper gastrocnemius and increases ankle dorsiflexion range — reduces strain on upper calf.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Wall):** Stand 1 metre from wall, right foot back, toes elevated on wall at knee height. **STEP 2 (Lean):** Lean body into wall keeping right heel on floor. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel intense stretch at upper calf. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: calf raise gastrocnemius warmup soleus
why: Progressively warms calf-Achilles unit through full plantar flexion before running, jumping, or sport.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand on both feet, hands on wall. **STEP 2 (Rise):** Rise up onto balls of feet as high as possible. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower slowly and controlled.
process: 20 reps x 2 sets. Build pace gradually.

common_name: downward dog calf gastrocnemius yoga stretch
why: Classic yoga inversion that passively loads and lengthens both calves using body weight.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Plank):** Start in high plank. **STEP 2 (Push):** Push hips up and back into inverted V shape. **STEP 3 (Press):** Actively press one heel at a time down toward floor. Alternate slowly.
process: 1 minute. Dog walk by alternating heel presses.

common_name: calf raise gastrocnemius soleus strength
why: Builds calf strength and Achilles tendon load capacity — primary preventive measure for calf strains and Achilles injuries.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand on edge of step or flat floor. **STEP 2 (Rise):** Rise to full tiptoe range. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower slowly (3 seconds). Add load by going single-leg as you progress.
process: 20 reps x 3 sets. Progress to single-leg x 15 reps.

common_name: single leg calf raise achilles soleus
why: Progressive Achilles tendon loading — builds the collagen remodelling needed to resolve chronic Achilles tendinopathy.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Step):** Stand on edge of step, one foot only. **STEP 2 (Rise):** Rise up to full tiptoe. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower SLOWLY over 3-4 seconds below step level.
process: 15 reps x 3 sets per foot, twice daily.

common_name: ankle circle tibialis fibular relief
why: Full circumduction of ankle joint mobilises all four ankle ligaments and promotes synovial fluid after sprain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit/Lie):** Sit or lie with leg elevated. **STEP 2 (Circle):** Make large slow circles with ankle — 10 clockwise. **STEP 3 (Reverse):** 10 counter-clockwise.

common_name: inner ankle medial tibialis stretch
why: Stretches medial deltoid ligament and tibialis posterior — relieves inner ankle tightness after over-pronation or medial sprain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with foot crossed over opposite knee. **STEP 2 (Hold):** Hold heel with one hand. **STEP 3 (Evert):** Use other hand to gently push sole of foot outward. Hold 20 seconds.

common_name: outer ankle peroneal fibular stretch
why: Stretches peroneal muscles on outer ankle — relieves soreness after lateral ankle sprain or peroneal tendinitis.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with foot on opposite knee. **STEP 2 (Invert):** Gently cup heel and turn sole of foot inward. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch on outer ankle. Hold 20 seconds.

common_name: front ankle tibialis anterior stretch
why: Stretches tibialis anterior along shin and front ankle — relieves shin splints and front-of-ankle impingement pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Kneel):** Kneel on soft surface, tops of feet flat. **STEP 2 (Sit):** Slowly sit back onto heels. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel stretch across tops of feet and front ankles. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: achilles ankle towel stretch gentle
why: Non-weight-bearing Achilles stretch — ideal for acute ankle pain where standing is too painful.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with legs extended. Loop towel around ball of foot. **STEP 2 (Pull):** Pull towel toward you, bringing foot toward shin. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold when gentle pull felt above heel. Hold 30 seconds.

common_name: ankle pump warmup tibialis peroneal
why: Rapidly cycles ankle through flexion and extension to pump blood into foot and warm ankle stabilisers.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with legs extended. **STEP 2 (Flex):** Point toes away — hold 1 second. **STEP 3 (Pull):** Pull toes toward you — hold 1 second. Alternate rapidly.

common_name: resistance band ankle eversion peroneal outer
why: Strengthens peroneal muscles to prevent repeat lateral ankle sprains — most important outer ankle rehab exercise.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Band):** Sit with resistance band around foot anchored to opposite leg. **STEP 2 (Evert):** Push sole of foot outward against band. **STEP 3 (Return):** Slowly return to neutral.

common_name: resistance band ankle inversion tibialis inner
why: Strengthens tibialis posterior and medial stabilisers — prevents flat-foot collapse and inner ankle rolling.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Band):** Sit with band around foot, anchored outward. **STEP 2 (Invert):** Pull sole of foot inward. **STEP 3 (Return):** Slowly return.

common_name: single leg balance ankle tibialis peroneal
why: Rebuilds proprioceptive (balance) system in ankle joint — most important factor in preventing repeated sprains.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand on one foot. **STEP 2 (Focus):** Keep ankle steady — resist wobbling. **STEP 3 (Progress):** Close eyes or stand on pillow once you can hold 30 seconds easily.
process: 30 seconds x 3 sets per leg. Daily.

common_name: plantar fascia heel stretch foot
why: Directly stretches plantar fascia at the calcaneal insertion — dramatically reducing plantar fasciitis morning pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Before getting out of bed, sit on edge. Cross right foot over left knee. **STEP 2 (Pull):** Use right hand to pull all five toes back toward shin. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Feel tight band along arch and deep heel. Hold 30 seconds.
process: 3 holds x 30 seconds — especially BEFORE first steps in the morning.

common_name: frozen bottle heel roll plantar fascia foot
why: Cold reduces heel inflammation while rolling provides plantar fascia massage — highly effective for acute heel pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Freeze):** Freeze a water bottle. **STEP 2 (Roll):** Sitting in chair, place frozen bottle under foot. **STEP 3 (Focus):** Slowly roll it along arch and concentrate pressure at painful heel area. Roll 5 minutes.
process: 5 minutes per foot. 2-3 times daily for acute pain.

common_name: tennis ball arch roll plantar foot
why: Deep tissue massage to entire plantar fascia from arch to toe — breaks adhesions and reduces morning stiffness.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand/Sit):** Place tennis ball under foot. **STEP 2 (Roll):** Apply comfortable downward pressure and slowly roll ball from heel to base of toes. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Pause 20-30 seconds on any tender spots.
process: 3-5 minutes per foot daily. Stand for stronger pressure.

common_name: towel scrunch arch intrinsic foot
why: Strengthens intrinsic foot muscles forming the arch — reduces arch fatigue and the collapsing that leads to plantar fasciitis.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Towel):** Place small towel flat on floor. **STEP 2 (Scrunch):** Using toes only, scrunch towel toward you. **STEP 3 (Release):** Straighten toes to push it back. Repeat.

common_name: metatarsal ball foot press massage
why: Releases tight interosseous muscles and reduces metatarsalgia pain across the ball of the foot.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Cross):** Sit and cross foot over opposite knee. **STEP 2 (Thumbs):** Place both thumbs under ball of foot. **STEP 3 (Press):** Apply firm circular pressure across all five metatarsal heads.

common_name: toe stretch big toe extension plantar foot
why: Stretches long toe flexors and plantar fascia simultaneously — relieves hammertoe tension and tight-toe sensation.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with foot on knee. **STEP 2 (Extend):** Pull all toes back toward shin as far as comfortable. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 20 seconds. Then pull each toe back individually.
process: 3 holds x 20 seconds together, then 10 seconds each toe.

common_name: intrinsic foot dome arch strengthening plantar
why: Most specific arch-strengthening exercise — contracts intrinsic muscles to lift arch without curling toes.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit with foot flat on floor. **STEP 2 (Shorten):** Pull ball of foot toward heel WITHOUT curling toes — feel arch lift. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 5 seconds.
process: 15 reps x 3 sets per foot. This takes practice — persevere.

common_name: standing heel drop calcaneal plantar heel
why: Eccentrically loads plantar fascia and Achilles at the heel, prompting tissue remodelling to resolve chronic heel pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Step):** Stand with toes on step edge, heels over edge. **STEP 2 (Rise):** Rise up on tiptoe. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Slowly lower BOTH heels below step level. Take 4 seconds.

common_name: toe tap warmup foot plantar toe
why: Activates intrinsic foot muscles and dorsiflexors, warming the foot before running or prolonged standing.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand tall. **STEP 2 (Tap):** Rapidly tap toes on floor, one foot at a time. **STEP 3 (Both):** Progress to tapping both feet alternately.

common_name: toe spread yoga foot intrinsic plantar
why: Reawakens intrinsic foot muscles and corrects toe crowding — reduces bunion and hammertoe pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Sit):** Sit comfortably. **STEP 2 (Spread):** Try to spread all five toes as wide apart as possible. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold spread for 5 seconds. Relax fully.
process: 10-15 reps per foot. Do barefoot daily.

common_name: hero pose foot plantar yoga ankle
why: Simultaneously stretches plantar fascia, toe extensors, and ankle — one of the best full-foot restoration poses.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Kneel):** Kneel on soft surface, toes tucked under. **STEP 2 (Sit):** Sit back onto heels, letting weight stretch plantar fascia. **STEP 3 (Hold):** Hold 1 minute. Rise slowly.
process: 1 minute. Build gradually over weeks if very tight.

common_name: marble pickup toe intrinsic foot strength
why: Challenges toe flexors individually — rebuilds fine motor strength needed to prevent toe cramping and plantar pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Scatter):** Scatter 10 small objects on floor. **STEP 2 (Pick):** Using toes only, pick up one marble and drop it into a cup. **STEP 3 (Repeat):** Pick up all 10.

common_name: short foot arch dome strengthening intrinsic
why: Progresses short foot exercise by adding a calf raise — trains arch under dynamic load for lasting plantar fascia health.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand barefoot. Activate short foot arch dome. **STEP 2 (Hold dome):** While maintaining arch dome, slowly rise onto tiptoe. **STEP 3 (Lower):** Lower slowly, keeping arch dome active throughout.
process: 15 reps x 3 sets. Progress to single-leg.

common_name: foot tripod alignment posture arch plantar
why: Teaches proper foot weight distribution (heel, first and fifth metatarsal heads) — corrects flat foot or high arch that drives plantar pain.
instructions: **STEP 1 (Stand):** Stand barefoot. **STEP 2 (Find):** Feel pressure at three points: heel, base of big toe, and base of little toe. **STEP 3 (Equal):** Adjust weight until all three points feel equally loaded.
process: Hold tripod position for 30 seconds x 5 reps. Check every time you stand barefoot.
